headline: Opportunity Party in kingmaker position as Luxon and Hipkins approval slumps
text: A new RNZ-Reid Research poll (1,000 respondents, online, 14–21 Aug, ±3.1% margin of error) has Labour on 32.2%, National 29.1%, NZ First 11.9%, Greens 10.2%, ACT 7.7%, and Opportunity on 5.3% (6 projected seats). Neither major bloc could govern without Opportunity's seats, and preferred PM is close: Hipkins 21.3%, Luxon 19.9% — both near record lows.

headline: National rules out bed tax and bank tax; mayors "disappointed"
text: PM Christopher Luxon pledged "no new taxes" if re-elected, dropping proposed accommodation and bank levies. Finance Minister Nicola Willis said an accommodation levy would inevitably raise costs for Kiwis booking a weekend away. Auckland Mayor Wayne Brown said he was disappointed, though outlets word his quote slightly differently ("deeply" vs. "extremely") — treat the exact wording as unconfirmed.

headline: ACT unveils "one law for all" policy targeting courts and Treaty clauses
text: Leader David Seymour announced a policy to stop courts treating tikanga as an independent legal source except where Parliament explicitly allows it, and to require Cabinet sign-off on bills referencing the Treaty of Waitangi. Seymour said tikanga "cannot be used to influence court decisions," except where Parliament has expressly allowed it.

headline: Expelled Te Pāti Māori MP Tākuta Ferris to stand as independent
text: Ferris, ousted from the party earlier this year, confirmed he will contest the Te Tai Tonga Māori seat as an independent candidate.
